stem.text: The function \( f \) is twice differentiable for all real \( x \), and its derivative is \( f'(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} + 3} \).

parts.prompt: Find all open intervals on which the graph of \( f \) is concave up. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: The denominator is positive, so f'' has the sign of 3 - x^2.

points.criterion: Gives the open interval -sqrt(3) < x < sqrt(3), written with or without its endpoints.
States that f' is increasing on that interval, or that f''(x) = (3 - x^2)/(x^2 + 3)^2 > 0 there.

parts.prompt: Find all open intervals on which the graph of \( f \) is concave down. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: f'' has the sign of 3 - x^2, which is negative when |x| > sqrt(3).

points.criterion: Gives the interval x < -sqrt(3), that is (-infinity, -sqrt(3)), with or without its endpoint.
Gives the interval x > sqrt(3), that is (sqrt(3), infinity), with or without its endpoint. Joining the two intervals into one does not earn this point.
States that f' is decreasing on these intervals, or that f''(x) < 0 there.

parts.prompt: Find all open intervals on which \( f \) is decreasing and the graph of \( f \) is concave down. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: f' < 0 exactly when x < 0, since the denominator is positive.
Intersect with the concave down intervals from part (b).

points.criterion: Gives the interval x < -sqrt(3), that is (-infinity, -sqrt(3)), with or without its endpoint, and no other interval.

States both that f' < 0 there (so f is decreasing) and that f' is decreasing there, or f'' < 0 (so the graph is concave down). A reason covering only one of the two conditions does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Find all open intervals on which \( f \) is increasing and the graph of \( f \) is concave up. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: Intersect with the concave up interval from part (a).

points.criterion: Gives the interval 0 < x < sqrt(3), with or without its endpoints, and no other interval.
States both that f' > 0 there (so f is increasing) and that f' is increasing there, or f'' > 0 (so the graph is concave up). A reason covering only one of the two conditions does not earn the point.
